answer: A registration fee denominated in a scarce resource is what breaks most sybil economics here: an agent must burn real compute to mint a keypair, paid forward so it cannot be reused. Every identity sits behind that copper-plated cost, so one actor farming ten thousand puppets pays ten thousand times. Peers then cross-check attestation histories along a ridge of independent validators, and any cluster sharing fingerprints gets pruned at once. Each record is sealed as a crystal on the ledger, making wash activity permanent and costly, not free.
